title: Numeric and Geometric Patterns: Linear and Geometric Sequences
seo_title: Grade 9 Numeric and Geometric Patterns Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate and extend numeric and geometric patterns looking for relationships between numbers, including patterns represented in physical or diagram form, patterns not limited to sequences involving a constant difference or ratio, represented in tables or algebraically; describe and justify the general rules for observed relationships between numbers in own words or in algebraic language.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 patterns worksheets: linear and geometric sequences, the general term and pattern problems. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A linear sequence has a constant difference: Tₙ = dn + c.
  • A geometric sequence has a constant ratio: 3, 6, 12, 24 … (× 2).
  • To find a far term, substitute n into the rule.
  • To check if a number is a term, solve for n.

Examples

Example

5, 8, 11, 14, …

d = 3

Tₙ = 3n + 2

Answer: T₅₀ = 152

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Linear or geometric?Check differences, then ratios.
Term or position?n is the position.
The constant3n + 2, not 3n.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 9 say about patterns?
faq.a: Investigate and extend numeric and geometric patterns, describe the general rule in algebraic language, and find terms.
Each term is multiplied by the same number.

faq.q: Can the ratio be a fraction?

items.q: What is the next term? 2, 8, 32, 128, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 4 each time. 128 × 4 = 512.

items.q: What is the next term? −2, 10, 22, 34, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 12 each time. 34 + 12 = 46.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, 20, 100, 500, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 500 × 5 = 2 500.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, 10, 100, 1 000, 10 000, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 10, so it is geometric.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 7, 21, 63, 189, 567, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 3, so it is geometric.

items.q: What is the next term? 14, 19, 24, 29, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 5 each time. 29 + 5 = 34.

items.q: What is the next term? 11, 14, 17, 20, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 3 each time. 20 + 3 = 23.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, 15, 75, 375, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 375 × 5 = 1 875.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? −3, −10, −17, −24, −31, …
items.e: The difference is always −7, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, −8, 16, −32, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by −2 each time. −32 × (−2) = 64.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 11, 9, 7, 5, 3, …
items.e: The difference is always −2, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 8, −1, −10, −19, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 9 each time. −19 − 9 = −28.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …
items.e: The differences change (3, 5, 7, 9) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, …
items.e: The differences change (9, 11, 13, 15) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? −1, 7, 15, 23, 31, …
items.e: The difference is always 8, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 0, −1, −2, −3, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 1 each time. −3 − 1 = −4.

items.q: What is the next term? 1, 4, 16, 64, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 4 each time. 64 × 4 = 256.

items.q: What is the next term? −5, −13, −21, −29, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 8 each time. −29 − 8 = −37.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, …
items.e: The differences change (5, 7, 9, 11) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, −2, 4, −8, 16, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × −2, so it is geometric.

items.q: What is the nth term of −14, −19, −24, −29, …?
items.e: The difference is −5, so start with −5n. The 1st term of −5n is −5; to get −14, subtract 9. −5n − 9.

items.q: What is the nth term of 2, 8, 14, 20, …?
items.e: The difference is 6, so start with 6n. The 1st term of 6n is 6; to get 2, subtract 4. 6n − 4.

items.q: What is the nth term of −7, −4, −1, 2, …?
items.e: The difference is 3, so start with 3n. The 1st term of 3n is 3; to get −7, subtract 10. 3n − 10.

items.q: What is the nth term of 8, 10, 12, 14, …?
items.e: The difference is 2, so start with 2n. The 1st term of 2n is 2; to get 8, add 6. 2n + 6.

items.q: What is the nth term of −3, −11, −19, −27, …?
items.e: The difference is −8, so start with −8n. The 1st term of −8n is −8; to get −3, add 5. −8n + 5.

items.q: What is the nth term of 6, 15, 24, 33, …?
items.e: The difference is 9, so start with 9n. The 1st term of 9n is 9; to get 6, subtract 3. 9n − 3.

items.q: What is the nth term of 15, 27, 39, 51, …?
items.e: The difference is 12, so start with 12n. The 1st term of 12n is 12; to get 15, add 3. 12n + 3.

items.q: What is the nth term of −4, 2, 8, 14, …?
items.e: The difference is 6, so start with 6n. The 1st term of 6n is 6; to get −4, subtract 10. 6n − 10.

items.q: What is the nth term of −2, −1, 0, 1, …?
items.e: The difference is 1, so start with n. The 1st term of n is 1; to get −2, subtract 3. n − 3.

items.q: What is the nth term of −5, −1, 3, 7, …?
items.e: The difference is 4, so start with 4n. The 1st term of 4n is 4; to get −5, subtract 9. 4n − 9.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 21, 31, 41, 51, …
items.e: The difference is 10, so the sequence is like 10n. The zero term is 21 − 10 = 11. So the nth term is 10n + 11.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence −6, −9, −12, −15, …
items.e: The difference is −3, so the sequence is like −3n. The zero term is −6 + 3 = −3. So the nth term is −3n − 3.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 5, 13, 21, 29, …
items.e: The difference is 8, so the sequence is like 8n. The zero term is 5 − 8 = −3. So the nth term is 8n − 3.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 1, 6, 11, 16, …
items.e: The difference is 5, so the sequence is like 5n. The zero term is 1 − 5 = −4. So the nth term is 5n − 4.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 10, 20, 30, 40, …
items.e: The difference is 10, so the sequence is like 10n. The zero term is 10 − 10 = 0. So the nth term is 10n.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 12, 21, 30, 39, …
items.e: The difference is 9, so the sequence is like 9n. The zero term is 12 − 9 = 3. So the nth term is 9n + 3.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence −7, −5, −3, −1, …
items.e: The difference is 2, so the sequence is like 2n. The zero term is −7 − 2 = −9. So the nth term is 2n − 9.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 17, 22, 27, 32, …
items.e: The difference is 5, so the sequence is like 5n. The zero term is 17 − 5 = 12. So the nth term is 5n + 12.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …
items.e: The difference is 3, so the sequence is like 3n. The zero term is 2 − 3 = −1. So the nth term is 3n − 1.

items.q: Find the nth term of the sequence 3, 10, 17, 24, …
items.e: The difference is 7, so the sequence is like 7n. The zero term is 3 − 7 = −4. So the nth term is 7n − 4.

items.q: What is the common ratio of 6, 60, 600, 6 000, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: 60 ÷ 6 = 10.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 1 600, 800, 400, 200, …
items.e: 200 ÷ 2 = 100. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 4th term is 16. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 3 times: 16 ÷ 8 = 2.

items.q: The sequence 1, 2, 4, … is geometric. What is the 6th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. The 6th term is 32.

items.q: The sequence 1, 2, 4, … is geometric. What is the 7th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. The 7th term is 64.

items.q: The sequence 5, 15, 45, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 3: 5, 15, 45, 135, 405. The 5th term is 405.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 5th term is 64. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 4 times: 64 ÷ 16 = 4.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 10. Its 5th term is 10 000. What is its 1st term?
What is the common ratio of 5, 10, 20, 40, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

items.q: What is the common ratio of 4, −12, 36, −108, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: −12 ÷ 4 = −3.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 2. The next term is 16.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 3, 30, 300, 3 000, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 10. The next term is 30 000.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 160, 80, 40, 20, …?
items.e: Each term is half of the one before. The next term is 10.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 2, 6, 18, 54, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 3. The next term is 162.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 1, 10, 100, 1 000, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 10. The next term is 10 000.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 2, 4, 8, 16, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 2. The next term is 32.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 1 000, 500, 250, 125, …?
items.e: Each term is half of the one before. The next term is 62,5.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 3, 9, 27, 81, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 3. The next term is 243.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 5, 50, 500, 5 000, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 10. The next term is 50 000.

items.q: What is the next term in the sequence 5, 10, 20, 40, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before multiplied by 2. The next term is 80.

items.q: A sequence has nth term 5n. Which term is equal to 170?
A sequence has nth term 8n + 6. Is 60 a term in the sequence?
c: Yes, because it is bigger than 8
No, because n would not be a whole number
items.e: 8n + 6 = 60 gives n = 54 ÷ 8, which is not a whole number. So no.

items.q: A sequence has nth term 8n − 1. Which term is equal to 159?
A sequence has nth term 4n − 8. What is the 18th term?
A sequence has nth term 2n − 6. Which term is equal to 60?
A sequence has nth term 5n − 5. Is 93 a term in the sequence?
c: No, because n would not be a whole number
Yes, because it is bigger than 5
items.e: 5n − 5 = 93 gives n = 98 ÷ 5, which is not a whole number. So no.

items.q: A sequence has nth term 3n − 8. Which term is equal to 112?
A sequence has nth term 8n + 6. Which term is equal to 102?
A sequence has nth term 8n − 7. What is the 34th term?
A sequence has nth term 8n + 4. What is the 59th term?
The nth term of a sequence is 6n + 7. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 6n + 7 = 157 gives n = (157 − 7) ÷ 6 = 25, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 157.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 5n + 1. Which term is equal to 41?
items.e: 5n + 1 = 41, so 5n = 40 and n = 8. It is the 8th term.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 4n + 3. Which term is equal to 95?
items.e: 4n + 3 = 95, so 4n = 92 and n = 23. It is the 23rd term.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 8n − 3. Which term is equal to 205?
items.e: 8n − 3 = 205, so 8n = 208 and n = 26. It is the 26th term.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 3n − 2. Which term is equal to 115?
items.e: 3n − 2 = 115, so 3n = 117 and n = 39. It is the 39th term.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 7n − 1. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 7n − 1 = 265 gives n = (265 + 1) ÷ 7 = 38, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 265.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 8n + 6. Which term is equal to 118?
items.e: 8n + 6 = 118, so 8n = 112 and n = 14. It is the 14th term.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 8n − 4. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 8n − 4 = 268 gives n = (268 + 4) ÷ 8 = 34, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 268.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 4n − 5. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 4n − 5 = 67 gives n = (67 + 5) ÷ 4 = 18, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 67.

items.q: The nth term of a sequence is 4n + 4. Which of these numbers is in the sequence?
items.e: 4n + 4 = 96 gives n = (96 − 4) ÷ 4 = 23, a whole number. The others do not give whole numbers. So 96.

items.q: What is the next term of the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?
items.e: Add the two terms before: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: What is the 10th square number?
What is the next triangular number? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences go up by 1: +2, +3, +4, +5, so add 6: 21.

items.q: What is the next cube number? 1, 8, 27, 64, …
A bacteria population doubles every hour. It starts at 50. How many are there after 5 hours?
items.e: 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 → 1 600. This is a geometric sequence with ratio 2.

items.q: A ball is dropped from 200 cm. Each bounce reaches half the height of the one before. How high is the 3rd bounce?
Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. How many sticks are in pattern 20?
items.e: The nth term is 3n + 1. Pattern 20: 3 × 20 + 1 = 61.

items.q: Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. Which pattern uses 100 sticks?
The nth term of a sequence is 50 − 4n. What is the first negative term?
Which sequence has the nth term 5 − 2n?
The patterns are made from matchsticks. How many matchsticks are in Pattern 10?
items.e: The sticks go 4, 7, 10, … so the nth term is 3n + 1. Pattern 10: 3 × 10 + 1 = 31.

items.q: The patterns are made from matchsticks. How many matchsticks are in Pattern 25?
items.e: The sticks go 4, 7, 10, … so the nth term is 3n + 1. Pattern 25: 3 × 25 + 1 = 76.

items.q: The patterns are made from matchsticks. What is the nth term for the number of matchsticks?
items.e: 4, 7, 10, … goes up by 3, and the zero term is 1: 3n + 1.

items.q: The patterns are made from matchsticks. Which pattern uses 61 matchsticks?
Which of these is the sequence of square numbers?
items.e: Square numbers are 1², 2², 3², …: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.

items.q: Which of these is the sequence of triangular numbers?
items.e: Triangular numbers add 2, then 3, then 4, …: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.

items.q: What is the next term in the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?
items.e: Each term is the sum of the two before: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: What is the next term? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences are 2, 3, 4, 5, so add 6: 15 + 6 = 21.

items.q: Which sequence is geometric?
items.e: In a geometric sequence you multiply by the same number each time (here × 2): 3, 6, 12, 24, ….

items.q: Which sequence is arithmetic (linear)?
items.e: An arithmetic sequence goes up or down by the same amount (here − 3): 20, 17, 14, 11, ….
